title.narrative: Carter Center:Advancing Participatory Rights of Women & Youth in Zambia II(2023)
Carter Center:Advancing Participatory Rights of Women & Youth in Zambia II(2023)

description.narrative: Detta projekt syftar till att stödja Carter Center och dess CSO-partners att utnyttja handlingskraftiga evenemang för att förespråka förändringar i policy och praxis genom användning av internationella instrument för mänskliga rättigheter och evenemang på hög nivå som toppmötet för demokrati för att bidra till att öka kvinnor och politiskt deltagande för ungdomar i Zambia.

This project is aimed at supporting the Carter Center and its CSO partners to leverage action-forcing events to advocate for policy and practice change through the use of international human rights instruments and high level events such as the Summit for democracy to contribute towards increasing women and youth political participation in Zambia.

Project Goal: Carter Center CSO partners leverage action-forcing events to advocate for policy and practice change.
Objective 1: By July 2023, CSO partners and their CBO members have increased capacity to utilize international human rights mechanisms to effectively advocate with government and key institutions tasked with protecting and promoting women and youth political participation.
Objective 2: Implementing partners shared participatory rights, good governance and human rights priorities amplified through high-level public discourse in association with S4D Summit.

Building on the capacity developed in implementing partners under the Advancing Participatory Rights of Women and Youth in Zambia phase I; Carter Center (CC) and its CSO partners sought to ''leverage action-forcing events to advocate for policy and practice change'' for increased political participation for women, youth and the disabled. Having trained the CSOs on how to use international human rights mechanisms to advocate and demand for human rights, each CSO partner submitted a CSO shadow report to the UPR, and the Zambia Center for Social Development (ZCSD) led a combined CSO effort to submit a shadow report on Zambia's performance on the International Covenant on Civil and Political Rights (ICCPR). Young Women in Action and Chapter One Foundation officially complained against the Zambian government to the African Commission on Human and People's Rights over the lack of diversity in appointing people to public office in January, 2022.
During phase II the focus was on advancing advocacy around the Universal periodic review (January 30, 2023); International Covenant on Civil and Political Rights (ICCPR) review (February 27 to March 24, 2023); the fifth African Youth Sustainable Development Goals (SDG) Summit (August, 2023); and the Summit for Democracy which took place in Lusaka (March 29 to 30, 2023).
CSO partners and their CBO members have increased capacity to utilize international human rights mechanisms to effectively advocate with government and key institutions tasked with protecting and promoting women, persons with disabilities and youth political participation.
Carter Center provided partners NGOCC, YWA, and ZCSD sub-awards to raise awareness on the findings and recommendations presented in their civil society reports to UN Human Rights mechanisms; and undertook advocacy efforts with government representatives and elected officials to gain support for adopting and implementing key recommendations for Zambia. Policy priorities included advocacy for operationalizing the Gender Equality and Equity Commission, establishing an effective gender machinery, achieving sustainable development goals that promote the participation of youth and women, and addressing societal, economic, and other barriers that hinder the political participation of women, youth, and persons with disabilities.
A position paper was agreed upon by stakeholders with three proposals for a politically strategic, stronger, well funded and accountable gender machinery or institutional arrangement for the actualisation of women's rights in Zambia. This paper will be used for advocacy even after the end of the project. Collaboration and consensus on the need for a Gender Ministry was attained among like-minded CSOs during the implementation of the project with the Carter Center playing a facilitative role.
Sub-grantee activities implemented by NGOCC, YWA, and ZCSD included protecting and promoting the political participation of women and youth through raising awareness of the review mechanisms and report findings, mobilizing support for implementing the policy recommendations emerging from the processes, and direct engagement with government officials urging support for relevant policy compliance and reforms.
The local partners engaged reached the following: 15 CSOs active at the national level 64 CBO and community women and youth leaders 19 media outlets with more than an estimated 4 million people reached More than 6000 people on social media 7 MPs, including members of the Womens Parliamentary Caucus Representatives from 5 Government Ministries/divisions. 2 Traditional Leaders 235 university students
The above activities were collectively implemented in seven provinces: Lusaka, Central, Copperbelt, North-Western, Southern, Eastern, Luapula; and nine Districts: Mufulira, Mpika, Kabwe, Livingstone, Lusaka, Chongwe, Chipata, Lundazi, and Mansa.
This fostered policy dialogue and exchange of ideas between policy makers and CSOs on the UPR recommendations from national to sub-national levels. Experiences from other countries were also shared through regional experts and knowledge sharing by the Cater Center. This strengthened awareness and demand for the Government to adhere to international human rights standards regarding the need for women, people with disabilities and youth to participate equitably in national development and political leadership.
Implementing partners shared participatory rights, good governance, and human rights priorities amplified through high-level public discourse in association with Summit for Democracy (S4D).
Taking advantage of the Summit for Democracy that was held in Lusaka and Co-hosted by the United States Government and Government of Zambia, the Cater Center in collaboration with the Swedish Embassy, Irish Embassy, Finish Embassy and partner organizations, successfully held a side event during the Summit for Democracy on March 31, 2023. CC partners played critical roles in implementing the side event, including providing input into the program design and Outcomes Document which has become a tool for advocacy. More than 170 participants from government and quasi-government bodies, civil society organizations (CSO), international non-governmental organizations (INGO), and bilateral and multilateral donor agencies explored various issues affecting the participation of women, youth, and PWDs in electoral processes and decision-making during four interactive panel discussions.
Some of the results attributed to the S4D side event included:
- Increased public discourse on democracy and good governance.
- Amplification of the voices of Zambian and other African elected leaders and civil society leaders with a broader audience.
- Increased knowledge among Zambia implementing partners and their peers of comparative experiences to advance women and youth political participation and other human rights.
- CSO and CBO leaders have strengthened their capacity to use human rights mechanisms, individually and jointly, to advance their work to increase the political participation of women, youth, and persons with disabilities.
- Heightened awareness among CSOs, university students, and the general public about the correlation between support for the participation of women and international human rights standards ratified by Zambia.
- Affirmation by the Minister of Justice of the Zambian Government's dedication to implementing Human Rights Committee recommendations, focusing on addressing gender-based violence.
Youth Side Event at the African Youth SDG Summit
On August 16, 2023, Carter Center partner Alliance for Accountability Advocates Zambia (AAAZ) hosted a side event at the African Youth SDG Summit to facilitate discussions on enhancing meaningful youth participation in democracy and achieving SDGs in Zambia and the region. This provided opportunities for youth to learn from various continental counterparts who attended the summit. The event brought together Zambia and regional experts to provide comparative, in-depth information on the select topics such as governance, climate change, gender equality and political participation. Establishing a youth consortium to advance calls for affirmative action measures and other youth rights concerns was discussed to sustain UPR-related advocacy.
Summit for Democracy (S4D) Post-Event Consultations
The Center organized several consultations with key stakeholders in follow-up to the March 31, 2023, S4D Side Event. Sessions explored societal barriers to participation in more detail with focus on marriage, impacts of education status, violence against women in elections (VAWE), the role of traditional leaders, the gender machinery in Zambia and the role of political parties. A wide range of civil society, government officials, academia, and bi- and multi-lateral donors participated in the sessions. These sessions helped to concretise and contextualize some strategies for CSOs to continue with their advocacy work. More importantly, the sessions also increased CSOs knowledge on promoting women, youth and disabled participatory rights.
No indicator available - only a description of the activity results is published
